examples.hard: He tied a sharp hook to his line, and within minutes the first fish had taken the bait.

examples.easy: What sort of music do you like?

examples.hard: What sort of people are the customers in your favourite shop, and why do you think they keep coming back?

examples.normal: We learned how to subtract numbers from each other in class.
examples.hard: If you subtract your monthly expenses from your salary, you'll see exactly how much you can afford to save.

examples.normal: The knots were so tight that I couldn't untie them.
examples.hard: Make sure the lid of the jar is tight, otherwise the food will go off within days.

examples.normal: Because he's popular, Joe is the virtual leader of the group.

examples.normal: George's fishing rod could even weigh the fish he caught.

examples.normal: We have to whisper in the library so people can read.

examples.easy: People tend to eat too fast.

examples.easy: Chemistry is a closed book to me.

examples.easy: I like mustard on my sandwich.

examples.hard: Why does the burning feeling from mustard disappear much faster than the heat you get from chillies?

examples.normal: The lecture was so abstruse that half the audience fell asleep.
examples.hard: The magazine answers readers' questions on all kinds of abstruse scientific topics that most people never think about.

examples.normal: Shops reduce prices on products that are close to their sell-by date.
examples.hard: Many people throw food away once the sell-by date has passed, although it is often still perfectly safe to eat.

examples.easy: This yoghurt is past its use-by date.

examples.normal: Fresh shellfish should be eaten on the day you buy it.

examples.normal: Dirty hands can easily contaminate food in a busy kitchen.

examples.easy: Plants produce oxygen during the day.

examples.hard: Fruit kept in sealed bags lasts longer because the reduced amount of oxygen slows down the process of ripening.

examples.easy: The old apples began to decay.

examples.easy: Please go on with your story.

examples.hard: Engineers calculated the ideal number of teeth on a bottle cap by taking its circumference into account.

examples.easy: They paid homage to the inventor.
examples.normal: The film pays homage to the great directors of the past.
examples.hard: Next time you open a bottle, pay homage to the engineers who worked out the perfect design for its cap.

examples.easy: A correspondent wrote to the magazine.
examples.normal: Several correspondents sent letters disagreeing with the article.
examples.hard: The magazine's correspondents concluded that feeding the whole planet on a vegetarian diet would be possible but difficult.

examples.normal: Ploughing the fields used to be done with horses.
examples.hard: Ploughing dead plants back into the soil helps to keep it rich in the nutrients that future crops will need.

examples.normal: Heavy rain this summer has damaged many of the crops.
examples.hard: Farmers in dry regions need to grow crops that take in very little water but still produce a good harvest.

examples.easy: He is on a business trip.

examples.hard: If I weren't going on a business trip next week, I would have accepted that new assignment yesterday.

examples.normal: I was surprised when he accepted my invitation to dinner.
examples.hard: If the salary had been a little higher, I would have accepted their offer without thinking twice.

examples.easy: My boss gave me an assignment.

examples.hard: She turned down the overseas assignment because she didn't want to be away from her family for a year.

examples.normal: If you have a headache, an aspirin might help a little.
examples.hard: If Sam had taken an aspirin earlier, she wouldn't have such a terrible headache now.

examples.normal: Staring at a computer screen all day gives me a headache.
examples.hard: After the long meeting he had such a bad headache that he went home and lay down.

examples.normal: The doctor changed my medication because it made me tired.
examples.hard: If Anthony had taken the medication as prescribed, he wouldn't be lying sick in bed today.

examples.normal: My GP prescribed a stronger cream for the rash on my arm.
examples.hard: Doctors are being urged to prescribe antibiotics less often because overuse is making bacteria resistant.

examples.easy: That sounds like a reasonable plan.
examples.normal: It is reasonable to expect a reply within two working days.
examples.hard: If she had taken reasonable precautions, she wouldn't be dealing with all these problems now.

examples.hard: As a precaution, the airline cancelled all flights until the storm had passed and the runway was safe again.

examples.hard: Pregnant women are advised to rest more and avoid lifting heavy objects during the last months.

examples.normal: The police caught the car thief two streets away.
examples.hard: If old Sam hadn't chased the car thief, he wouldn't have suffered a heart attack and would still be alive.

examples.normal: Regular exercise reduces the risk of having a heart attack.
examples.hard: My uncle completely changed his diet and lifestyle after suffering a mild heart attack at the age of fifty.

examples.easy: Is the old cat still alive?
examples.normal: Luckily, all the passengers were alive after the crash.
examples.hard: Doctors said he would still be alive today if he had gone to hospital as soon as the pain started.

examples.easy: She is blind to his faults.
examples.normal: Parents are sometimes blind to the problems their children have.
examples.hard: If Polly hadn't been so blind to Jack's faults, she would have realised he was trying to cheat her.

examples.easy: He swindled her out of money.

examples.hard: Jack was out to swindle her from the start, but she was too much in love to notice.

examples.normal: He needs a diploma to apply for that teaching job.
examples.hard: If Jillian had studied harder at school, she would have a diploma now and a much better job.

examples.normal: Please fill in the application form and return it by Friday.
examples.hard: If Nick had turned in his application on time, he would probably be working for the company now.

examples.normal: The children do their chores before they can watch TV.
examples.hard: If Natalie and Liz had finished their chores earlier, they would be able to relax and watch a film now.

examples.normal: My grandfather buys a lottery ticket every Saturday morning.
examples.hard: If we had won the lottery last night, we would be rich now and planning a trip around the world.

examples.normal: If I were him, I wouldn't quit before finding another job.
examples.hard: He quit his well-paid job in the city to open a small café in the village where he grew up.

examples.easy: We only eat here on special occasions.
examples.normal: My mother wears her best dress only for special occasions.
examples.hard: Describe a special occasion when you had a really enjoyable meal and explain why it was so memorable.

examples.easy: It was a very enjoyable evening.

examples.hard: The conference was surprisingly enjoyable, mainly because the speakers were funny and the food was excellent.

examples.normal: My favourite meal of the day is a big breakfast.
examples.hard: The meal we had on my grandmother's birthday was the most enjoyable one I can remember.

units.name: Lesson 99 - Money, work and city life

examples.easy: The idea really appeals to me.
examples.normal: Working from home appeals to many parents with young children.
examples.hard: The new smartphone was designed to appeal to older users who find modern technology confusing.

examples.easy: I assume you know the plan.

examples.normal: She borrowed her brother's car for the weekend trip.

examples.normal: Our lawyer meets new clients every Monday morning.

examples.normal: We took a taxi from the airport to the downtown area.

examples.normal: The lecture was so dull that half the students fell asleep.

examples.normal: He was embarrassed when he forgot his manager's name.

examples.normal: Train fares go up again at the start of next year.

examples.normal: The hotel, a former castle, was built two centuries ago.

examples.normal: There is no simple formula for success in business.

examples.normal: Her grandfather founded a small bank in the town centre.

examples.normal: My uncle invested all his savings in a new restaurant.
examples.hard: Governments that invest heavily in education usually see stronger economic growth in the long term.

examples.easy: I got a loan from the bank.

examples.hard: Without a student loan, she would never have been able to afford to study medicine at university.

examples.normal: Learning English is practical because you can use it everywhere.

examples.easy: He paid a quarter for gum.

examples.hard: He found an old quarter in his coat pocket and used it to buy a newspaper from the machine.

examples.normal: He moved to a new company for a better salary.
examples.hard: Although the salary was lower, she accepted the job because it offered more freedom and shorter hours.

examples.normal: He got a full scholarship to study engineering in London.
examples.hard: Without a scholarship, many talented students from poor families could never afford a university education.

examples.easy: She found a temporary job for the summer.
examples.normal: The office is closed for temporary repairs this week.
examples.hard: She took a temporary position at the bank, hoping it would eventually lead to a permanent contract.

examples.normal: Divers discovered treasure on an old ship under the sea.
examples.hard: Local legend says that pirates buried their treasure somewhere on the island, but nobody has ever found it.

examples.normal: The doctor urged her to stop smoking immediately.
examples.hard: Police are urging drivers to avoid the motorway this weekend because of serious roadworks near the airport.

examples.easy: Each child got a small portion.

examples.hard: Third culture kids spend a significant portion of their developmental years in a culture outside their parents' own.

examples.easy: Food prices rose exponentially last year.
examples.normal: The number of online shoppers has grown exponentially since 2020.
examples.hard: As international travel becomes cheaper, the number of children growing up between cultures is increasing exponentially.

examples.normal: Teachers need to understand the cultural complexity of their classes.
examples.hard: The cultural complexity of her childhood in four countries made 'Where are you from?' hard to answer.

examples.normal: The relevance of this research to everyday life is clear.
examples.hard: Critics questioned the relevance of the study, arguing that its findings could not be applied outside the laboratory.

examples.normal: Young folk today spend most of their free time online.
examples.hard: The sociologist discovered that folk who moved abroad had created a lifestyle different from both their home and host cultures.

examples.easy: An expatriate family moved next door.
examples.normal: Many expatriate families send their children to international schools.
examples.hard: In the 1950s, most expatriate families had parents from the same culture who stayed in one host country.

examples.normal: Thousands of students go overseas to study every year.
examples.hard: While her parents were working overseas, she was looked after by her grandparents back home in Tashkent.

examples.normal: The cultural differences inside her family were almost invisible to outsiders.
examples.hard: While racial diversity may be recognised, the hidden cultural diversity of her life remained largely invisible to others.

examples.normal: The country has made progress in reducing racial inequality.
examples.hard: Friendships that cross racial, national and social barriers teach young people how differently others see the world.

examples.normal: Her best-selling book has been translated into thirty languages.
examples.hard: The author of a best-selling book about Liberia grew up in Niger before moving there as a teenager.

examples.easy: She has a great capacity for work.
examples.normal: Children have an amazing capacity to learn new languages.
examples.hard: Adults who grew up between cultures often show a remarkable capacity to understand people from very different backgrounds.

examples.easy: The refugees needed food and shelter.
examples.normal: Thousands of refugees crossed the border to escape the war.
examples.hard: Many children of refugees experience the same cultural challenges as third culture kids, even though they never chose to move.

examples.normal: The adoptee finally met her birth mother at the age of thirty.
examples.hard: International adoptees often grow up wondering which culture they really belong to and how to describe their identity.

examples.normal: The company offers cross-cultural training to staff working abroad.
examples.hard: Cross-cultural kids can act as bridges between worlds that traditionally would never have connected with each other.

examples.easy: He has a strong national identity.
examples.normal: Moving between countries can make young people question their identity.
examples.hard: Researchers are rethinking traditional ways of defining diversity and identity in an increasingly mobile and connected world.

examples.easy: Please state your ethnicity on the form.
examples.normal: People of every ethnicity live together in this neighbourhood.
examples.hard: Their friendship is based on shared experience rather than shared nationality, religion or ethnicity.

examples.easy: The house has a communal kitchen.
examples.normal: Students share a communal garden behind the main building.
examples.hard: Moving countries often brings challenges to a child's personal, communal and professional life that last for many years.

units.name: Lesson 101 - Passives and everyday phrases with in

examples.normal: She was offered a place at three different universities.

examples.easy: We were stuck in a traffic jam.

examples.normal: Alex got stung by a wasp while sitting in the garden.

examples.easy: We live in a quiet suburb.
examples.normal: Many families move to the suburbs to get a bigger garden.
examples.hard: In one of the city's suburbs, huge tower blocks were built to house some of its poorer inhabitants.

examples.normal: The town's inhabitants voted against the new shopping centre.
examples.hard: The original inhabitants of the area were moved to new flats when the old houses were demolished.

examples.normal: My parents taught me the value of hard work.
examples.hard: The new houses that look old may represent a return to traditional tastes and values.

units.name: Lesson 104 - Reported speech and office work

examples.normal: In reported speech, the verb usually moves into the past.
examples.hard: When you tell a friend what someone said yesterday, you normally use reported speech instead of their exact words.

examples.easy: Put the words in quotation marks.
examples.normal: In writing, we use quotation marks to show direct speech.
examples.hard: If you copy a sentence from another author, put it in quotation marks and say where it comes from.

examples.normal: She felt ill after lunch, so she went home early.
examples.hard: He woke up feeling ill, so he phoned his manager and said he wouldn't be coming to work.

examples.easy: I can't afford a new car.
examples.normal: We want to go on holiday, but we can't afford it.
examples.hard: Many young couples can no longer afford to buy a flat in the city centre, so they rent instead.

examples.normal: Have you been to the cinema recently, or are you too busy?
examples.hard: Prices have risen sharply recently, so many families are having to cut back on what they spend.

examples.normal: The man on the reception desk gave us a map.
examples.hard: When we arrived at the hotel, nobody was at the reception desk, so we had to wait twenty minutes.

examples.easy: I get on with my boss.
examples.normal: Sarah gets on fine with all her new colleagues.
examples.hard: Although they disagree about politics, my brother and my husband get on with each other surprisingly well.

examples.easy: She lives next door to me.
examples.normal: The woman who lives next door is a doctor at the hospital.
examples.hard: When the family next door went on holiday, they asked us to water their plants and feed their cat.

examples.normal: Grace works for a company that makes office furniture.
examples.hard: After moving into the flat, they spent months choosing furniture that suited the small living room.

examples.easy: Can you recommend a good restaurant?
examples.normal: We stayed at the hotel that you recommended last summer.
examples.hard: The doctor recommended that he should change his diet and take more exercise if he wanted to feel better.

examples.easy: My cousin works as a tour guide.
examples.normal: John, who speaks French and Italian, works as a tour guide.
examples.hard: Our tour guide, who had lived in Rome all her life, knew a story about almost every building we passed.

examples.easy: My boss is in a bad mood.
examples.normal: Lisa, whose car had broken down, was in a very bad mood.
examples.hard: He's always in a bad mood on Monday mornings, so I try not to ask him for anything before lunch.

collocations: put someone in a bad mood

examples.easy: I need to change my diet.
examples.normal: The doctor told me to eat more vegetables in my diet.
examples.hard: A healthy diet, combined with regular exercise, can greatly reduce the risk of heart disease in later life.

examples.easy: My job involves a lot of travelling.
examples.normal: The project will involve working closely with other departments.
examples.hard: Being a personal assistant involves organising travel, setting up meetings and dealing with hundreds of emails.

examples.normal: The new stadium, which can hold 90,000 people, opens next month.
examples.hard: Thousands of fans gathered outside the stadium hours before the final, hoping to get a glimpse of the players.

examples.normal: The strike at the factory began ten days ago.
examples.hard: The train drivers' strike caused chaos for commuters, who had to find other ways to get to work.

examples.normal: A job was advertised, and a lot of people applied for it.
examples.hard: The company advertised the position in several national newspapers but received very few suitable applications.

examples.normal: Few of the applicants had the necessary qualifications for the job.
examples.hard: Without a recognised teaching qualification, it can be difficult to find a job in a state school.

examples.normal: The doctor who examined me couldn't find anything wrong.
examples.hard: Before buying a second-hand car, ask a mechanic to examine it carefully for any hidden problems.

examples.normal: The sun is one of millions of stars in the universe.
examples.hard: Scientists are still trying to understand how the universe began and whether life exists anywhere else in it.

examples.normal: Liz works as a personal assistant to the director of a school.
examples.hard: A good personal assistant can organise her boss's travel, meetings and documents without being reminded.

examples.normal: Could you book a hotel reservation for me in Paris next week?
examples.hard: If you cancel your hotel reservation less than twenty-four hours before arrival, you may have to pay a fee.

examples.normal: You have a budget for a one-day event, including food.
examples.hard: The organisers had to cut the entertainment because they had already spent most of the budget on food.

examples.normal: The ticket price includes food, drinks and entertainment.
examples.hard: For the end-of-year event, the students wanted live music and other entertainment rather than formal speeches.
